resource.name: aws_launch_template
resource.description: Provides an EC2 launch template resource. Can be used to create instances or auto scaling groups.
resource.llm_summary: The `aws_launch_template` resource enables the streamlined creation and management of EC2 instance configurations, serving as a reusable blueprint for deploying instances or auto scaling groups. It is commonly used for automating infrastructure provisioning, optimizing instance lifecycle management, and standardizing settings like AMI selection, instance types, networking, storage, and user data scripts. This resource is ideal for scenarios requiring consistent and scalable EC2 deployments, such as auto scaling, disaster recovery setups, or pre-configured environments for applications.

examples.title: Basic Usage
examples.llm_summary: This example demonstrates the basic configuration of the `aws_launch_template` resource, showcasing how to define key attributes for EC2 instance provisioning, including block device mappings, CPU options, instance type, metadata options, and user data. It illustrates advanced settings such as spot instance market options, API termination protection, security group associations, and tagging, providing a comprehensive template for flexible and optimized instance deployment.

arguments.name: default_version
arguments.description: (Optional) Default Version of the launch template.
arguments.llm_summary: The `default_version` argument in the `aws_launch_template` resource allows users to specify the default version of the launch template to be used when creating or managing instances. Setting this value ensures that a specific version is consistently applied, enabling precise control over instance configurations and simplifying version management for infrastructure deployments.

arguments.name: description
arguments.description: (Optional) Description of the launch template.
arguments.llm_summary: The `description` argument for the `aws_launch_template` resource allows users to define a human-readable summary or purpose for the launch template, aiding in identification and documentation of its intended use. While optional, setting this argument can improve resource management and clarity, especially in environments with multiple templates.

arguments.name: disable_api_stop
arguments.description: (Optional) If true, enables EC2 Instance Stop Protection.
arguments.llm_summary: The `disable_api_stop` argument in the `aws_launch_template` resource allows users to control EC2 Instance Stop Protection by specifying whether API calls to stop the instance are disabled. Setting this to `true` prevents the instance from being stopped via API actions, which is useful for ensuring critical workloads remain running and protected from accidental or unauthorized shutdowns.

arguments.name: disable_api_termination
arguments.description: (Optional) If `true`, enables EC2 Instance Termination Protection
arguments.llm_summary: The `disable_api_termination` argument in the `aws_launch_template` resource allows users to control whether EC2 instances launched from the template are protected from accidental termination via API calls. Setting this to `true` enables termination protection, which is useful for safeguarding critical instances in production environments or preventing unintended disruptions during automated workflows.

arguments.name: ebs_optimized
arguments.description: (Optional) If `true`, the launched EC2 instance will be EBS-optimized.
arguments.llm_summary: The `ebs_optimized` argument in the `aws_launch_template` resource allows users to specify whether the EC2 instances launched from the template should be optimized for Amazon Elastic Block Store (EBS) performance. Enabling this feature (`true`) configures the instance to use dedicated network bandwidth for EBS I/O, improving storage throughput and reducing latency, which is ideal for workloads requiring high disk performance.

arguments.name: id
arguments.llm_summary: The `id` argument represents the unique identifier of the `aws_launch_template` resource, which is automatically generated upon creation. While not configurable, it is commonly used for referencing the launch template in other resources or outputs, enabling integration and dependency management within Terraform configurations.

arguments.name: image_id
arguments.description: (Optional) The AMI from which to launch the instance or use a Systems Manager parameter convention e.g. `resolve:ssm:parameter-name`. See docs for more details.
arguments.llm_summary: The `image_id` argument in the `aws_launch_template` resource allows users to specify the Amazon Machine Image (AMI) or a Systems Manager parameter that defines the base operating system and software configuration for instances launched using the template. By setting this argument, users can control the foundational environment of their EC2 instances, enabling customization of workloads, application deployment, or infrastructure consistency across environments.

arguments.name: instance_initiated_shutdown_behavior
arguments.description: (Optional) Shutdown behavior for the instance. Can be `stop` or `terminate`. (Default: `stop`).
arguments.llm_summary: The `instance_initiated_shutdown_behavior` argument in the `aws_launch_template` resource allows users to define how an EC2 instance should behave when it is shut down from within the instance itself. By specifying either `stop` or `terminate` (default: `stop`), users can control whether the instance is preserved for later use or permanently deleted, enabling lifecycle management aligned with operational or cost optimization goals.

arguments.name: instance_type
arguments.description: (Optional) The type of the instance. If present then `instance_requirements` cannot be present.
arguments.llm_summary: The `instance_type` argument in the `aws_launch_template` resource allows users to specify the compute instance type (e.g., `t2.micro`, `m5.large`) for EC2 instances launched using the template. This defines the hardware configuration, including CPU, memory, and networking capacity, to meet workload requirements. Note that it cannot be used alongside `instance_requirements`, ensuring either explicit or flexible instance selection.

arguments.name: kernel_id
arguments.description: (Optional) The kernel ID.
arguments.llm_summary: The `kernel_id` argument in the `aws_launch_template` resource allows users to specify the kernel ID for the instance launched using the template. This enables customization of the operating system kernel, typically for advanced use cases such as running specialized workloads or custom kernels, providing greater control over the instance's runtime environment.

arguments.name: key_name
arguments.description: (Optional) The key name to use for the instance.
arguments.llm_summary: The `key_name` argument in the `aws_launch_template` resource allows users to specify the name of an existing SSH key pair to associate with instances launched using the template. This enables secure remote access to the instances by configuring the public key for authentication, aligning with common user goals of managing instance access and security.

arguments.name: name
arguments.description: (Optional) The name of the launch template. If you leave this blank, Terraform will auto-generate a unique name.
arguments.llm_summary: The `name` argument in the `aws_launch_template` resource allows users to define a custom, human-readable identifier for the launch template, facilitating easier organization and reference within AWS. If omitted, Terraform auto-generates a unique name, making this argument optional but useful for aligning templates with naming conventions or specific project requirements.

arguments.name: name_prefix
arguments.description: (Optional) Creates a unique name beginning with the specified prefix. Conflicts with `name`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `name_prefix` argument in the `aws_launch_template` resource allows users to define a unique name for the launch template that begins with a specified prefix, ensuring predictable naming conventions while avoiding conflicts with the `name` argument. This is particularly useful for dynamically generating resource names in environments where consistent naming patterns are required, such as multi-environment deployments or automated workflows.

arguments.name: ram_disk_id
arguments.description: (Optional) The ID of the RAM disk.
arguments.llm_summary: The `ram_disk_id` argument in the `aws_launch_template` resource allows users to specify the ID of a RAM disk to attach to instances launched using the template. This is typically used for specialized workloads or legacy systems that require a specific RAM disk, enabling users to customize the instance's boot configuration to meet unique application or environment requirements.

arguments.name: security_group_names
arguments.description: (Optional) A list of security group names to associate with. If you are creating Instances in a VPC, use `vpc_security_group_ids` instead.
arguments.llm_summary: Defines a set of security group names to associate with instances launched using the template, enabling network access control at the instance level. Typically used in non-VPC environments, as VPC-based instances should instead use `vpc_security_group_ids` for specifying security groups.

arguments.name: tags
arguments.description: (Optional) A map of tags to assign to the launch template. If configured with a provider `default_tags` configuration block present, tags with matching keys will overwrite those defined at the provider-level.
arguments.llm_summary: The `tags` argument in the `aws_launch_template` resource allows users to define a map of key-value pairs to assign metadata tags to the launch template. This enables users to organize, categorize, and manage resources effectively by applying custom identifiers, such as environment, project, or cost center, with the ability to override provider-level default tags if configured.

arguments.name: tags_all
arguments.llm_summary: The `tags_all` argument in the `aws_launch_template` resource allows users to define a comprehensive set of key-value tags that are automatically applied to the launch template and all associated resources created from it. This enables consistent tagging for resource organization, cost allocation, and governance, aligning with common user goals like enforcing tagging policies across cloud infrastructure.

arguments.name: update_default_version
arguments.description: (Optional) Whether to update Default Version each update. Conflicts with `default_version`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `update_default_version` argument in the `aws_launch_template` resource allows users to control whether the default version of the launch template is automatically updated to the latest version upon each modification. Enabling this behavior ensures the most recent configuration is used as the default, simplifying version management but conflicting with manual `default_version` settings.

arguments.name: user_data
arguments.description: (Optional) The base64-encoded user data to provide when launching the instance.
arguments.llm_summary: The `user_data` argument in the `aws_launch_template` resource allows users to specify base64-encoded scripts or configuration data that is executed during instance initialization. This enables automation of tasks such as setting environment variables, installing software, or configuring services, streamlining instance provisioning and ensuring consistent setup across deployments.

arguments.name: vpc_security_group_ids
arguments.description: (Optional) A list of security group IDs to associate with. Conflicts with `network_interfaces.security_groups`
arguments.llm_summary: The `vpc_security_group_ids` argument in the `aws_launch_template` resource allows users to specify a set of security group IDs to associate with the instances launched using the template. This configuration controls network-level access rules, enabling users to define inbound and outbound traffic permissions for the instances, which is essential for securing workloads and meeting compliance requirements.

blocks.name: block_device_mappings
blocks.description: (Optional) Specify volumes to attach to the instance besides the volumes specified by the AMI. See Block Devices below for details.

arguments.name: device_name
arguments.llm_summary: The `device_name` argument in the `block_device_mappings` block of the `aws_launch_template` resource allows users to specify the name of the device to be attached to the instance, such as `/dev/xvda` or `/dev/sdb`. By defining this, users can control how storage devices are mapped to the instance, enabling precise configuration of disk layouts for tasks like boot volumes, data storage, or application-specific requirements.

arguments.name: no_device
arguments.llm_summary: The `no_device` argument in the `block_device_mappings` block of the `aws_launch_template` resource allows users to specify whether a block device mapping should be suppressed or excluded from the instance configuration. By setting this argument, users can prevent the automatic attachment of a specific device, enabling customization of storage configurations to exclude unwanted volumes or override default mappings.

arguments.name: virtual_name
arguments.llm_summary: The `virtual_name` argument in the `block_device_mappings` block of the `aws_launch_template` resource allows users to specify a name for ephemeral (instance store) volumes attached to the instance. By setting this argument, users can define the logical identifier for the ephemeral storage, enabling configuration of temporary, high-performance storage typically used for caching or transient data during instance runtime.

blocks.name: ebs

arguments.name: delete_on_termination
arguments.llm_summary: The `delete_on_termination` argument in the `ebs` block of the `aws_launch_template` resource allows users to define whether the associated EBS volume should be automatically deleted when the instance using the launch template is terminated. Configuring this argument helps manage the lifecycle of EBS volumes, enabling users to control resource cleanup and avoid unnecessary storage costs.

arguments.name: encrypted
arguments.llm_summary: The `encrypted` argument in the `ebs` block of the `aws_launch_template` resource allows users to specify whether the EBS volume attached to the instance should be encrypted. Setting this argument enables data-at-rest encryption for the volume, enhancing security by protecting sensitive information and meeting compliance requirements.

arguments.name: iops
arguments.llm_summary: The `iops` argument in the `ebs` block of the `aws_launch_template` resource allows users to specify the number of input/output operations per second (IOPS) for the EBS volume, enabling fine-grained control over storage performance. This is particularly useful for provisioning high-performance volumes, such as those using the `io1` or `io2` volume types, to meet application-specific throughput and latency requirements.

arguments.name: kms_key_id
arguments.llm_summary: The `kms_key_id` argument in the `ebs` block of the `aws_launch_template` resource allows users to specify the AWS KMS key used to encrypt the EBS volumes created by the launch template. By setting this argument, users can enforce encryption for data at rest using a custom or default KMS key, aligning with security and compliance requirements for sensitive workloads.

arguments.name: snapshot_id
arguments.llm_summary: The `snapshot_id` argument in the `ebs` block of the `aws_launch_template` resource allows users to specify the ID of an existing EBS snapshot to initialize the volume. By setting this argument, users can create an EBS volume pre-populated with data from the specified snapshot, enabling scenarios like restoring data, cloning environments, or provisioning pre-configured storage for applications.

arguments.name: throughput
arguments.llm_summary: The `throughput` argument in the `ebs` block of the `aws_launch_template` resource allows users to specify the dedicated throughput in MiB/s for provisioned EBS volumes with the `io2` or `gp3` volume types. Configuring this parameter helps optimize performance for workloads requiring high and consistent disk throughput, such as large-scale databases or analytics applications.

arguments.name: volume_size
arguments.llm_summary: The `volume_size` argument in the `ebs` block of the `aws_launch_template` resource specifies the size (in GiB) of the EBS volume to be attached to the instance. This allows users to define the storage capacity for the volume, directly impacting the amount of data the instance can store and supporting common goals like configuring application storage or meeting performance requirements.

arguments.name: volume_type
arguments.llm_summary: The `volume_type` argument in the `ebs` block of the `aws_launch_template` resource allows users to specify the type of EBS volume to be attached to the instance, such as `gp2` (general-purpose SSD), `io1` (provisioned IOPS SSD), or `st1` (throughput-optimized HDD). Configuring this argument impacts storage performance and cost, enabling users to tailor the instance's disk characteristics to match workload requirements like high IOPS, throughput, or cost-efficiency.

blocks.llm_summary: The "ebs" configuration block within the "block_device_mappings" section of the "aws_launch_template" resource defines settings for Amazon Elastic Block Store (EBS) volumes attached to an instance. It encapsulates parameters such as volume size, type, encryption, and delete-on-termination behavior, enabling users to customize storage performance, security, and lifecycle management for instance-specific block devices. Configuring this block allows for precise control over EBS volume characteristics, ensuring optimal storage configurations tailored to application needs.

The `block_device_mappings` configuration block in the `aws_launch_template` resource defines custom storage volumes to attach to an instance, supplementing or overriding the default volumes provided by the AMI. It enables detailed control over block device settings, such as volume type, size, and encryption, allowing users to tailor instance storage configurations to meet specific performance, security, or capacity requirements.

blocks.name: capacity_reservation_specification
blocks.description: (Optional) Targeting for EC2 capacity reservations. See Capacity Reservation Specification below for more details.

arguments.name: capacity_reservation_preference
arguments.description: Indicates the instance's Capacity Reservation preferences. Can be `open` or `none`. (Default `none`).
arguments.llm_summary: The `capacity_reservation_preference` argument in the `capacity_reservation_specification` block of the `aws_launch_template` resource allows users to define how instances launched from the template interact with EC2 Capacity Reservations. By setting this argument to `open`, instances can utilize any available Capacity Reservation that matches their attributes, while `none` (default) ensures instances do not use Capacity Reservations, enabling users to control resource allocation strategies for cost optimization or workload placement.

blocks.name: capacity_reservation_target
blocks.description: Used to target a specific Capacity Reservation:  The capacity_reservation_target block supports the following:

arguments.name: capacity_reservation_id
arguments.description: The ID of the Capacity Reservation in which to run the instance.
arguments.llm_summary: The `capacity_reservation_id` argument allows users to specify the ID of a Capacity Reservation where the instance launched by the `aws_launch_template` should run, ensuring dedicated compute capacity is allocated for the instance. This configuration is useful for workloads requiring guaranteed resource availability within a specific Capacity Reservation.

arguments.name: capacity_reservation_resource_group_arn
arguments.description: The ARN of the Capacity Reservation resource group in which to run the instance.
arguments.llm_summary: Specifies the ARN of a Capacity Reservation resource group to control where the instance is launched, enabling users to target a specific group of reserved compute capacity for their workloads. This configuration helps ensure capacity availability within a predefined group, aligning with resource allocation and high-availability strategies.

blocks.llm_summary: The `capacity_reservation_target` block within the `capacity_reservation_specification` of the `aws_launch_template` resource is used to specify and target a particular Capacity Reservation for EC2 instances. It encapsulates settings that define the association with a specific reservation, enabling users to ensure instances are launched into pre-allocated capacity, optimizing resource availability and cost management in reserved environments.

The `capacity_reservation_specification` block in the `aws_launch_template` resource enables targeted management of EC2 capacity reservations, allowing users to specify how instances launched from the template utilize reserved capacity. This block encapsulates settings related to capacity reservation preferences, ensuring optimized resource allocation and availability for workloads requiring guaranteed compute capacity.

blocks.name: cpu_options
blocks.description: (Optional) The CPU options for the instance. See CPU Options below for more details.

arguments.name: amd_sev_snp
arguments.description: Indicates whether to enable the instance for AMD SEV-SNP. AMD SEV-SNP is supported with M6a, R6a, and C6a instance types only. Valid values are `enabled` and `disabled`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `amd_sev_snp` argument in the `cpu_options` block of the `aws_launch_template` resource allows users to specify whether to enable AMD Secure Encrypted Virtualization-Secure Nested Paging (SEV-SNP) for the instance. This feature enhances security by providing memory encryption and integrity protection, and it is supported only on specific instance types (M6a, R6a, C6a). Valid values are `enabled` or `disabled`, enabling users to configure advanced security features for workloads requiring enhanced data protection.

arguments.name: core_count
arguments.description: The number of CPU cores for the instance.
arguments.llm_summary: "Defines the number of physical CPU cores allocated to an instance, allowing users to optimize compute performance for workloads requiring specific core counts. This argument is part of the `cpu_options` configuration and is typically used to tailor instance hardware to match application requirements, such as high-performance computing or parallel processing tasks."

arguments.name: threads_per_core
arguments.description: The number of threads per CPU core. To disable Intel Hyper-Threading Technology for the instance, specify a value of 1. Otherwise, specify the default value of 2. Both number of CPU cores and threads per core must be specified. Valid number of CPU cores and threads per core for the instance type can be found in the CPU Options Documentation
arguments.llm_summary: The `threads_per_core` argument in the `cpu_options` block of the `aws_launch_template` resource allows users to configure the threading behavior of the instance's CPU cores by specifying the number of threads per core. This setting enables control over Intel Hyper-Threading Technology, where a value of `1` disables hyper-threading for single-threaded performance optimization, and a value of `2` enables hyper-threading for multi-threaded workloads, aligning with the instance type's supported CPU configurations.

blocks.llm_summary: "Defines CPU options for instances launched via the `aws_launch_template`, enabling control over processor configurations such as core and thread count. This block allows users to optimize instance performance and tailor compute resources to workload requirements."

blocks.name: credit_specification
blocks.description: (Optional) Customize the credit specification of the instance. See Credit Specification below for more details.

arguments.name: cpu_credits
arguments.description: The credit option for CPU usage. Can be `standard` or `unlimited`. T3 instances are launched as `unlimited` by default. T2 instances are launched as `standard` by default.
arguments.llm_summary: The `cpu_credits` argument in the `credit_specification` block of the `aws_launch_template` resource allows users to define the CPU credit configuration for burstable EC2 instances (e.g., T2 and T3). By specifying `standard` or `unlimited`, users can control whether the instance operates with capped burst performance or unlimited CPU usage, impacting cost and performance optimization based on workload requirements.

blocks.llm_summary: The `credit_specification` block in the `aws_launch_template` resource allows users to configure the CPU credit options for burstable performance instances (T-series). This block enables fine-grained control over instance performance by specifying whether the instance operates in standard or unlimited mode, optimizing cost and performance for workloads with variable CPU usage.

blocks.name: elastic_gpu_specifications
blocks.description: (Optional) DEPRECATED The elastic GPU to attach to the instance. See Elastic GPU below for more details.

arguments.name: type
arguments.llm_summary: The `type` argument in the `elastic_gpu_specifications` block of the `aws_launch_template` resource specifies the type of Elastic GPU to attach to the instance, allowing users to define the GPU's capabilities for graphics acceleration. Setting this argument ensures the instance is equipped with the appropriate GPU resources to support workloads like 3D rendering, visualization, or other GPU-intensive applications.

blocks.llm_summary: The `elastic_gpu_specifications` block in the `aws_launch_template` resource configures the attachment of Elastic GPUs to an EC2 instance, enabling enhanced graphical processing capabilities for workloads requiring GPU acceleration. This block encapsulates settings related to GPU allocation, helping users optimize instance performance for graphics-intensive applications or machine learning tasks.

blocks.name: elastic_inference_accelerator
blocks.description: (Optional) DEPRECATED Configuration block containing an Elastic Inference Accelerator to attach to the instance. See Elastic Inference Accelerator below for more details.

arguments.name: type
arguments.description: (Required) Accelerator type.
arguments.llm_summary: The `type` argument for the `elastic_inference_accelerator` block in the `aws_launch_template` resource specifies the type of Elastic Inference Accelerator to attach to the instance, enabling users to define the level of GPU-powered inference performance for machine learning workloads. Setting this argument ensures the instance is provisioned with the appropriate accelerator type to optimize cost and performance for AI/ML applications.

blocks.llm_summary: The `elastic_inference_accelerator` block in the `aws_launch_template` resource configures the attachment of Elastic Inference Accelerators to instances, enabling cost-effective acceleration for machine learning inference workloads. This block encapsulates settings related to the type and configuration of the accelerator, allowing users to optimize performance for AI/ML applications while managing resource efficiency.

blocks.name: enclave_options
blocks.description: (Optional) Enable Nitro Enclaves on launched instances. See Enclave Options below for more details.

arguments.name: enabled
arguments.description: If set to `true`, Nitro Enclaves will be enabled on the instance. For more information, see the documentation on Nitro Enclaves.
arguments.llm_summary: The `enabled` argument in the `enclave_options` block of the `aws_launch_template` resource allows users to control whether Nitro Enclaves are activated for instances launched using the template. Setting this argument to `true` enables secure, isolated compute environments designed for sensitive data processing, aligning with user goals like enhancing security and workload isolation.

blocks.llm_summary: The `enclave_options` block in the `aws_launch_template` resource enables and manages Nitro Enclaves on instances launched using the template. It encapsulates settings related to secure, isolated compute environments for sensitive workloads, allowing users to configure advanced security features for data protection and cryptographic operations.

blocks.name: hibernation_options
blocks.description: (Optional) The hibernation options for the instance. See Hibernation Options below for more details.

arguments.name: configured
arguments.description: If set to `true`, the launched EC2 instance will hibernation enabled.
arguments.llm_summary: The `configured` argument in the `hibernation_options` block of the `aws_launch_template` resource enables users to specify whether launched EC2 instances should support hibernation. Setting this to `true` ensures the instance can be paused and resumed, which is useful for preserving the instance state across stops and starts, aligning with cost-saving and state retention goals.

blocks.llm_summary: The `hibernation_options` block in the `aws_launch_template` resource configures instance hibernation settings, enabling the ability to pause and resume instances while preserving their in-memory state. This block is used to define hibernation-related parameters, allowing users to optimize instance lifecycle management for workloads requiring fast recovery and state persistence.

blocks.name: iam_instance_profile
blocks.description: (Optional) The IAM Instance Profile to launch the instance with. See Instance Profile below for more details.

arguments.name: arn
arguments.llm_summary: The `arn` argument in the `iam_instance_profile` block of the `aws_launch_template` resource allows users to specify the Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of an IAM instance profile to associate with EC2 instances launched using the template. By setting this argument, users can define the IAM permissions and roles that the instances will inherit, enabling secure access to AWS resources and services based on the specified profile.

arguments.name: name
arguments.description: (Optional) The name of the launch template. If you leave this blank, Terraform will auto-generate a unique name.
arguments.llm_summary: The `name` argument in the `iam_instance_profile` block of the `aws_launch_template` resource allows users to specify a custom name for the launch template, providing a human-readable identifier for easier organization and management of cloud infrastructure. If left unset, Terraform auto-generates a unique name, which is useful for scenarios where explicit naming is not required or when avoiding naming conflicts.

blocks.llm_summary: The `iam_instance_profile` block in the `aws_launch_template` resource specifies the IAM Instance Profile to associate with launched EC2 instances, enabling the assignment of AWS permissions via attached IAM roles. This configuration is essential for managing instance-level access to AWS services, ensuring secure and controlled resource interactions.

blocks.name: instance_market_options
blocks.description: (Optional) The market (purchasing) option for the instance. See Market Options below for details.

arguments.name: market_type
arguments.llm_summary: The `market_type` argument in the `instance_market_options` block of the `aws_launch_template` resource allows users to specify whether the instance operates in the On-Demand or Spot market. Configuring this argument enables users to optimize cost by selecting Spot instances for variable workloads or On-Demand instances for predictable, uninterrupted usage, aligning with budget and availability requirements.

blocks.name: spot_options

arguments.name: block_duration_minutes
arguments.llm_summary: The `block_duration_minutes` argument in the `spot_options` block of the `aws_launch_template` resource allows users to specify the duration, in minutes, for which a Spot Instance is reserved. By setting this value, users can define a fixed time window (e.g., 60 or 120 minutes) for the instance's lifecycle, ensuring predictable cost and availability for workloads that require short-term compute capacity without interruptions.

arguments.name: instance_interruption_behavior
arguments.llm_summary: The `instance_interruption_behavior` argument in the `spot_options` block of the `aws_launch_template` resource allows users to define how a Spot Instance should respond when interrupted, specifying whether it should terminate, stop, or hibernate. This configuration helps users manage the lifecycle and recovery behavior of Spot Instances during interruptions, aligning with workload resilience and cost optimization goals.

arguments.name: max_price
arguments.llm_summary: The `max_price` argument in the `spot_options` block of the `aws_launch_template` resource allows users to specify the maximum hourly price they are willing to pay for Spot Instances. By setting this value, users can control cost limits for Spot Instance provisioning, ensuring that instances are only launched if the Spot market price is within their defined budget.

arguments.name: spot_instance_type
arguments.llm_summary: The `spot_instance_type` argument in the `spot_options` block of the `aws_launch_template` resource allows users to specify the type of Spot Instance request, such as "one-time" or "persistent." This configuration determines the behavior of the Spot Instance request, enabling users to control whether the instance runs until manually terminated or automatically re-requested after interruption, aligning with workload requirements and cost optimization strategies.

arguments.name: valid_until
arguments.llm_summary: The `valid_until` argument in the `spot_options` block of the `aws_launch_template` resource allows users to specify the expiration timestamp for the associated Spot Instance request. By setting this argument, users can define a lifecycle constraint, ensuring that the Spot Instance request automatically terminates after the specified time, which is useful for managing cost, resource availability, or time-bound workloads.

blocks.llm_summary: The `spot_options` configuration block within the `instance_market_options` of the `aws_launch_template` resource defines settings for managing Spot Instance behavior, including bid strategies, interruption handling, and allocation preferences. By configuring this block, users can optimize cost savings and control the lifecycle of Spot Instances, ensuring tailored behavior for workloads running in the AWS Spot market.

"Defines purchasing options for instances within the `aws_launch_template`, enabling configuration of market-related settings such as spot instance behavior. This block allows users to optimize costs and manage instance availability by specifying market preferences like spot pricing strategies and allocation policies."

blocks.name: instance_requirements
blocks.description: (Optional) The attribute requirements for the type of instance. If present then `instance_type` cannot be present.

arguments.name: accelerator_manufacturers
arguments.description: (Optional) List of accelerator manufacturer names. Default is any manufacturer. `Valid names: * amazon-web-services * amd * nvidia * xilinx`Copy
arguments.llm_summary: The `accelerator_manufacturers` argument in the `instance_requirements` block of the `aws_launch_template` resource allows users to specify a set of preferred hardware accelerator manufacturers (e.g., AWS, NVIDIA, AMD, Xilinx) for EC2 instances. This enables fine-grained control over the selection of instance types with compatible accelerators, aligning with workload requirements such as machine learning, high-performance computing, or GPU-intensive tasks.

arguments.name: accelerator_names
arguments.description: (Optional) List of accelerator names. arguments.description: (Optional) Associate a Carrier IP address with `eth0` for a new network interface. Use this option when you launch an instance in a Wavelength Zone and want to associate a Carrier IP address with the network interface. Boolean value, can be left unset.
arguments.llm_summary: The `associate_carrier_ip_address` argument in the `network_interfaces` block of the `aws_launch_template` resource allows users to specify whether to associate a Carrier IP address with the primary network interface (`eth0`) of an instance launched in a Wavelength Zone. This enables connectivity through a Carrier IP, typically used for low-latency applications in edge computing scenarios.

arguments.name: associate_public_ip_address
arguments.description: (Optional) Associate a public ip address with the network interface. Boolean value, can be left unset.
arguments.llm_summary: Controls whether the network interface in the launch template is assigned a public IP address upon instance creation. Setting this argument to `true` enables public internet access for the instance, typically used for scenarios requiring external connectivity, such as hosting web applications or accessing public APIs.

arguments.name: delete_on_termination
arguments.description: (Optional) Whether the network interface should be destroyed on instance termination.
arguments.llm_summary: The `delete_on_termination` argument in the `network_interfaces` block of the `aws_launch_template` resource allows users to define the lifecycle behavior of a network interface by specifying whether it should be automatically deleted when the associated EC2 instance is terminated. This configuration is useful for managing resource cleanup and ensuring ephemeral network interfaces are not retained unnecessarily, aligning with common goals of resource lifecycle management and cost optimization.

arguments.name: description
arguments.description: (Optional) Description of the network interface.
arguments.llm_summary: The `description` argument for the `network_interfaces` block in the `aws_launch_template` resource allows users to specify a human-readable text that describes the purpose or role of the network interface within the launch template. This helps document the configuration for clarity and aids in identifying the network interface's function in multi-interface setups or complex environments.

arguments.name: device_index
arguments.description: (Optional) The integer index of the network interface attachment.
arguments.llm_summary: The `device_index` argument in the `network_interfaces` block of the `aws_launch_template` resource allows users to specify the integer index that determines the attachment order of a network interface to the instance. By configuring this argument, users can control the mapping of network interfaces to specific device slots, enabling precise network interface placement for multi-interface instances or custom networking setups.

arguments.name: interface_type
arguments.description: (Optional) The type of network interface. To create an Elastic Fabric Adapter (EFA), specify `efa`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `interface_type` argument in the `network_interfaces` block of the `aws_launch_template` resource allows users to specify the type of network interface to attach to an instance, such as enabling advanced networking capabilities by selecting `efa` for Elastic Fabric Adapter (EFA). Configuring this argument is typically used to optimize high-performance computing (HPC) workloads or applications requiring low-latency, high-bandwidth network communication.

arguments.name: ipv4_address_count
arguments.description: (Optional) The number of secondary private IPv4 addresses to assign to a network interface. Conflicts with `ipv4_addresses`
arguments.llm_summary: "Configures the number of secondary private IPv4 addresses to automatically assign to a network interface within the launch template, enabling users to define additional IP capacity for workloads requiring multiple private addresses. This argument is useful for scaling network connectivity and conflicts with manually specifying individual IPs via `ipv4_addresses`."

arguments.name: ipv4_addresses
arguments.description: (Optional) One or more private IPv4 addresses to associate. Conflicts with `ipv4_address_count`
arguments.llm_summary: The `ipv4_addresses` argument allows users to explicitly specify one or more private IPv4 addresses to associate with a network interface in the launch template. This provides fine-grained control over IP address assignment, enabling users to define static IPs for instances, which is useful for scenarios requiring predictable network configurations or integration with existing systems.

arguments.name: ipv4_prefix_count
arguments.description: (Optional) The number of IPv4 prefixes to be automatically assigned to the network interface. Conflicts with `ipv4_prefixes`
arguments.llm_summary: "Defines the number of IPv4 prefixes to be automatically assigned to a network interface within the launch template, enabling dynamic allocation of IP address ranges for enhanced scalability and network configuration flexibility. Conflicts with `ipv4_prefixes`, ensuring users choose between automatic prefix assignment or manual specification."

arguments.name: ipv4_prefixes
arguments.description: (Optional) One or more IPv4 prefixes to be assigned to the network interface. Conflicts with `ipv4_prefix_count`
arguments.llm_summary: "Defines one or more specific IPv4 address prefixes to be assigned to a network interface within the launch template, enabling precise control over IP address allocation for the interface. This argument is useful for configuring custom network setups or ensuring compatibility with predefined subnet or routing requirements, and it cannot be used simultaneously with `ipv4_prefix_count`."

arguments.name: ipv6_address_count
arguments.description: (Optional) The number of IPv6 addresses to assign to a network interface. Conflicts with `ipv6_addresses`
arguments.llm_summary: The `ipv6_address_count` argument in the `network_interfaces` block of the `aws_launch_template` resource allows users to specify the number of IPv6 addresses automatically assigned to a network interface. This configuration is useful for enabling IPv6 connectivity in environments where dynamic address allocation is preferred, and it simplifies network setup by avoiding manual assignment of individual IPv6 addresses.

arguments.name: ipv6_addresses
arguments.description: (Optional) One or more specific IPv6 addresses from the IPv6 CIDR block range of your subnet. Conflicts with `ipv6_address_count`
arguments.llm_summary: The `ipv6_addresses` argument in the `network_interfaces` block of the `aws_launch_template` resource allows users to explicitly define one or more IPv6 addresses to assign to the network interface from the subnet's IPv6 CIDR block. This enables precise control over IP addressing for instances launched with the template, supporting scenarios like custom networking configurations or compliance with specific addressing schemes. Note that it conflicts with `ipv6_address_count`, which provides automatic assignment.

arguments.name: ipv6_prefix_count
arguments.description: (Optional) The number of IPv6 prefixes to be automatically assigned to the network interface. Conflicts with `ipv6_prefixes`
arguments.llm_summary: "Defines the number of IPv6 prefixes to be automatically assigned to a network interface within the launch template, enabling dynamic IPv6 address allocation for enhanced scalability and connectivity in IPv6-enabled environments. Conflicts with manual prefix specification via `ipv6_prefixes`, ensuring users can choose between automated or explicit configuration."

arguments.name: ipv6_prefixes
arguments.description: (Optional) One or more IPv6 prefixes to be assigned to the network interface. Conflicts with `ipv6_prefix_count`
arguments.llm_summary: The `ipv6_prefixes` argument allows users to specify one or more IPv6 address prefixes to assign to a network interface within an AWS Launch Template, enabling precise control over IPv6 addressing for instances. This configuration is useful for defining custom IPv6 network ranges, supporting advanced networking setups, and ensuring compatibility with IPv6-enabled environments, but it cannot be used in conjunction with `ipv6_prefix_count`.

arguments.name: network_card_index
arguments.description: (Optional) The index of the network card. Some instance types support multiple network cards. The primary network interface must be assigned to network card index 0. The default is network card index 0.
arguments.llm_summary: "Defines the index of the network card to which a network interface is attached, enabling configuration of multi-network card setups for instance types that support them. Typically used to specify the primary network interface (index 0) or assign additional interfaces to secondary network cards for advanced networking scenarios."

arguments.name: network_interface_id
arguments.description: (Optional) The ID of the network interface to attach.
arguments.llm_summary: The `network_interface_id` argument allows users to specify the ID of an existing network interface to attach to the launch template's instance configuration. By defining this, users can control the network connectivity of the instance, such as associating it with a pre-configured network interface for specific IP addresses, security groups, or subnet settings, enabling precise customization of network behavior and resource association.

arguments.name: primary_ipv6
arguments.description: (Optional) Whether the first IPv6 GUA will be made the primary IPv6 address.
arguments.llm_summary: The `primary_ipv6` argument in the `network_interfaces` block of the `aws_launch_template` resource allows users to specify whether the first IPv6 Global Unicast Address (GUA) assigned to the network interface should be designated as the primary IPv6 address. Configuring this argument impacts how IPv6 traffic is routed and prioritized, enabling users to define the primary address for applications or services requiring IPv6 connectivity.

arguments.name: private_ip_address
arguments.description: (Optional) The primary private IPv4 address.
arguments.llm_summary: The `private_ip_address` argument in the `network_interfaces` block of the `aws_launch_template` resource allows users to specify the primary private IPv4 address for the associated network interface. By setting this argument, users can control the static private IP assignment for the instance, ensuring predictable network communication and alignment with specific subnet or application requirements, such as fixed addressing for internal services or security configurations.

arguments.name: security_groups
arguments.description: (Optional) A list of security group IDs to associate.
arguments.llm_summary: The `security_groups` argument in the `network_interfaces` block of the `aws_launch_template` resource allows users to specify a set of security group IDs to control inbound and outbound traffic for the associated network interfaces. By defining this argument, users can enforce network access rules, such as restricting access to specific IP ranges or ports, to align with security and compliance requirements for their cloud environment.

arguments.name: subnet_id
arguments.description: (Optional) The VPC Subnet ID to associate.
arguments.llm_summary: The `subnet_id` argument in the `network_interfaces` block of the `aws_launch_template` resource allows users to specify the VPC Subnet ID where the network interface will be provisioned. By setting this argument, users can control the placement of the instance within a specific subnet, enabling network segmentation, access control, and alignment with security or routing requirements in their cloud environment.

blocks.name: connection_tracking_specification
blocks.description: (Optional) The Connection Tracking Configuration for the network interface. See Amazon EC2 security group connection tracking  The ena_srd_specification block supports the following:

arguments.name: tcp_established_timeout
arguments.description: (Optional) Timeout (in seconds) for idle TCP connections in an established state. Min: 60 seconds. Max: 432000 seconds (5 days). Default: 432000 seconds. Recommended: Less than 432000 seconds.
arguments.llm_summary: The `tcp_established_timeout` argument in the `connection_tracking_specification` of the `aws_launch_template` resource allows users to define the idle timeout duration (in seconds) for established TCP connections before they are terminated. By configuring this value, users can optimize connection tracking behavior to balance resource utilization and connection persistence, aligning with application-specific requirements for network performance and reliability.

arguments.name: udp_stream_timeout
arguments.description: (Optional) Timeout (in seconds) for idle UDP flows that have seen traffic only in a single direction or a single request-response transaction. Min: 30 seconds. Max: 60 seconds. Default: 30 seconds.
arguments.llm_summary: The `udp_stream_timeout` argument in the `connection_tracking_specification` of the `aws_launch_template` resource allows users to define the idle timeout duration (in seconds) for UDP flows that involve unidirectional traffic or single request-response transactions. By configuring this value, users can optimize connection tracking behavior for UDP streams, balancing resource efficiency and responsiveness in network traffic management.

arguments.name: udp_timeout
arguments.description: (Optional) Timeout (in seconds) for idle UDP flows classified as streams which have seen more than one request-response transaction. Min: 60 seconds. Max: 180 seconds (3 minutes). Default: 180 seconds.
arguments.llm_summary: The `udp_timeout` argument in the `connection_tracking_specification` of the `aws_launch_template` resource allows users to configure the idle timeout duration (in seconds) for UDP flows classified as streams with multiple request-response transactions. By setting this value, users can control how long idle UDP connections are retained before being terminated, optimizing connection tracking behavior for applications with specific network traffic patterns.

blocks.llm_summary: The `connection_tracking_specification` block within the `network_interfaces` configuration of the `aws_launch_template` resource defines settings for managing connection tracking behavior, such as handling stateful or stateless packet flows. This block enables fine-grained control over how network traffic is tracked and processed, optimizing security and performance for EC2 instances by leveraging features like enhanced connection tracking or specific configurations for ENA SRD (Scalable Reliable Datagram).

blocks.name: ena_srd_specification
blocks.description: (Optional) Configuration for Elastic Network Adapter (ENA) Express settings. Applies to network interfaces that use the ena Express feature. See details below.

arguments.name: ena_srd_enabled
arguments.description: (Optional) Whether to enable ENA Express. ENA Express uses AWS Scalable Reliable Datagram (SRD) technology to improve the performance of TCP traffic.
arguments.llm_summary: The `ena_srd_enabled` argument in the `ena_srd_specification` block of the `aws_launch_template` resource allows users to control whether ENA Express, powered by AWS Scalable Reliable Datagram (SRD) technology, is enabled for enhanced TCP traffic performance. Enabling this feature optimizes network throughput and reduces latency, making it ideal for workloads requiring high-speed and reliable data transmission.

blocks.name: ena_srd_udp_specification
blocks.description: (Optional) Configuration for ENA Express UDP optimization. See details below.  The ena_srd_udp_specification block supports the following:

arguments.name: ena_srd_udp_enabled
arguments.description: (Optional) Whether to enable UDP traffic optimization through ENA Express. Requires `ena_srd_enabled` to be `true`. NOTE: ENA Express requires specific instance types and minimum bandwidth of 25 Gbps. The connection_tracking_specification block supports the following:
arguments.llm_summary: The `ena_srd_udp_enabled` argument in the `ena_srd_udp_specification` block of the `aws_launch_template` resource allows users to enable UDP traffic optimization via ENA Express for supported EC2 instances. This enhances network performance for UDP workloads but requires `ena_srd_enabled` to be `true`, specific instance types, and a minimum network bandwidth of 25 Gbps.

blocks.llm_summary: The `ena_srd_udp_specification` block within the `ena_srd_specification` configuration of the `aws_launch_template` resource enables fine-tuned control over ENA Express UDP optimization settings, enhancing network performance for UDP traffic in EC2 instances. This block encapsulates related settings that optimize data transfer efficiency and reliability for applications relying on UDP, helping users achieve improved throughput and reduced latency in high-performance networking scenarios.

The `ena_srd_specification` block within the `network_interfaces` configuration of the `aws_launch_template` resource enables advanced settings for Elastic Network Adapter (ENA) Express, optimizing high-performance, low-latency networking for supported instances. It encapsulates related parameters to fine-tune ENA Express features, allowing users to enhance network throughput and reliability for workloads requiring accelerated data transfer.

The "network_interfaces" configuration block in the "aws_launch_template" resource allows users to define and customize the network interfaces attached to an instance at launch. It encapsulates settings related to network connectivity, such as interface properties, security groups, and subnet associations, enabling detailed control over instance-level networking to meet specific connectivity, security, and performance requirements.

blocks.name: placement
blocks.description: (Optional) The placement of the instance. See Placement below for more details.

arguments.name: affinity
arguments.description: (Optional) The affinity setting for an instance on a Dedicated Host.
arguments.llm_summary: The `affinity` argument in the `placement` block of the `aws_launch_template` resource allows users to specify the instance's affinity relationship with a Dedicated Host, enabling control over whether the instance is explicitly associated with a specific host. Configuring this argument helps optimize resource allocation and ensures consistent placement for workloads requiring host-level affinity, such as licensing or performance-sensitive applications.

arguments.name: availability_zone
arguments.description: (Optional) The Availability Zone for the instance.
arguments.llm_summary: Specifies the Availability Zone where the instance will be launched, allowing users to control the geographic placement of their resources for purposes such as reducing latency, achieving high availability, or meeting compliance requirements. If not set, the placement is determined automatically based on other configuration parameters.

arguments.name: group_name
arguments.description: (Optional) The name of the placement group for the instance.
arguments.llm_summary: The `group_name` argument in the `placement` block of the `aws_launch_template` resource allows users to specify the name of a placement group for the instance, enabling control over how instances are clustered within the AWS infrastructure. By setting this argument, users can optimize instance placement for specific workloads, such as achieving low-latency communication or high availability, aligning with goals like performance tuning or fault tolerance.

arguments.name: host_id
arguments.description: (Optional) The ID of the Dedicated Host for the instance.
arguments.llm_summary: The `host_id` argument in the `placement` block of the `aws_launch_template` resource allows users to specify the ID of a Dedicated Host on which the instance will be launched. This enables precise control over instance placement, typically used to optimize resource allocation, ensure compliance with licensing requirements, or achieve cost efficiency by utilizing pre-allocated Dedicated Hosts.

arguments.name: host_resource_group_arn
arguments.description: (Optional) The ARN of the Host Resource Group in which to launch instances.
arguments.llm_summary: Defines the ARN of the Host Resource Group where instances will be launched, enabling users to specify dedicated host placement for instances to optimize resource allocation, improve performance, or meet compliance requirements. This argument is typically used to configure instance placement within a managed group of dedicated hosts for enhanced control over infrastructure.

arguments.name: partition_number
arguments.description: (Optional) The number of the partition the instance should launch in. Valid only if the placement group strategy is set to partition.
arguments.llm_summary: "Defines the specific partition within a partition placement group where the instance will be launched, enabling users to control instance distribution for workload isolation or fault tolerance in partitioned cluster environments. Applicable only when the placement group strategy is set to 'partition.'"

arguments.name: spread_domain
arguments.description: (Optional) Reserved for future use.
arguments.llm_summary: The `spread_domain` argument in the `placement` block of the `aws_launch_template` resource is reserved for future use and does not currently enable any specific functionality. It is intended to potentially support advanced placement strategies, such as controlling the distribution of instances across failure domains or other logical groupings, aligning with user goals of optimizing availability and fault tolerance.

arguments.name: tenancy
arguments.description: (Optional) The tenancy of the instance (if the instance is running in a VPC). Can be `default`, `dedicated`, or `host`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `tenancy` argument in the `placement` block of the `aws_launch_template` resource allows users to specify the instance's tenancy type within a VPC, controlling whether the instance runs on shared (`default`), dedicated (`dedicated`), or host-specific (`host`) hardware. This configuration impacts resource isolation and cost, enabling users to align instance placement with compliance, performance, or cost optimization goals.

blocks.llm_summary: The "placement" configuration block in the "aws_launch_template" resource defines instance placement settings, such as availability zone, affinity, and tenancy, enabling control over where and how instances are deployed within AWS infrastructure. Configuring this block helps users optimize resource distribution, enforce tenancy policies, and align instance placement with specific architectural or cost requirements.

blocks.name: private_dns_name_options
blocks.description: (Optional) The options for the instance hostname. The default values are inherited from the subnet. See Private DNS Name Options below for more details.

arguments.name: enable_resource_name_dns_a_record
arguments.description: (Optional) Indicates whether to respond to DNS queries for instance hostnames with DNS A records.
arguments.llm_summary: Controls whether DNS A records are created for instance hostnames in the private DNS namespace, enabling users to configure DNS resolution for instances launched with the template. Setting this argument to `true` ensures instances can be resolved by their hostnames via DNS queries, supporting network connectivity and hostname-based access within private environments.

arguments.name: enable_resource_name_dns_aaaa_record
arguments.description: (Optional) Indicates whether to respond to DNS queries for instance hostnames with DNS AAAA records.
arguments.llm_summary: Controls whether the launch template's private DNS name options respond to DNS queries for instance hostnames with AAAA records, enabling IPv6 address resolution. This argument allows users to configure DNS behavior for instances, supporting environments that require IPv6 connectivity.

arguments.name: hostname_type
arguments.description: (Optional) The type of hostname for Amazon EC2 instances. For IPv4 only subnets, an instance DNS name must be based on the instance IPv4 address. For IPv6 native subnets, an instance DNS name must be based on the instance ID. For dual-stack subnets, you can specify whether DNS names use the instance IPv4 address or the instance ID. Valid values: `ip-name` and `resource-name`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `hostname_type` argument in the `private_dns_name_options` block of the `aws_launch_template` resource allows users to specify the type of DNS hostname assigned to Amazon EC2 instances. It controls whether the instance's private DNS name is based on its IPv4 address (`ip-name`) or its instance ID (`resource-name`), enabling users to align DNS naming behavior with the network configuration of their subnets (e.g., IPv4-only, IPv6-native, or dual-stack).

blocks.llm_summary: The `private_dns_name_options` block in the `aws_launch_template` resource configures hostname-related settings for instances, allowing users to define how private DNS names are assigned and resolved. It encapsulates options for customizing instance hostnames, overriding default subnet behavior, and enabling granular control over DNS naming conventions to align with specific networking requirements.

blocks.name: tag_specifications
blocks.description: (Optional) The tags to apply to the resources during launch. See Tag Specifications below for more details. Default tags are currently not propagated to ASG created resources so you may wish to inject your default tags into this variable against the relevant child resource types created.

arguments.name: resource_type
arguments.description: (Optional) The type of resource to tag.
arguments.llm_summary: The `resource_type` argument in the `tag_specifications` block of the `aws_launch_template` resource allows users to specify the type of AWS resource (e.g., instance, volume) to which the defined tags should be applied. By setting this argument, users can ensure that tags are consistently associated with specific resource types, enabling streamlined resource organization, cost tracking, and policy enforcement across their infrastructure.

arguments.name: tags
arguments.description: (Optional) A map of tags to assign to the resource.
arguments.llm_summary: The `tags` argument within `tag_specifications` for the `aws_launch_template` resource allows users to define a map of key-value pairs to assign metadata tags to associated AWS resources created by the launch template (e.g., EC2 instances, volumes). This enables users to organize, categorize, and manage resources effectively by specifying attributes like environment, cost center, or application, supporting common goals such as resource tracking, automation, and cost allocation.

blocks.llm_summary: The `tag_specifications` block in the `aws_launch_template` resource allows users to define tags that are applied to specific resource types created during instance launch, such as volumes or network interfaces. This block enables granular control over resource tagging, helping users organize, track, and manage cloud resources effectively, especially in scenarios where default tags are not automatically propagated to Auto Scaling Group (ASG)-created resources.

attributes.description: Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the launch template.
